quote: W = (M + Λ)⁻¹ Tᵀ C⁻¹ with Λ the inverse typical powers. Sources the cap resolves are canceled
discrepancy: None in the mathematics or the code. Two nuances: (1) the off-diagonal feature covariance uses trigamma(B·T) times the squared normalized cross-power; the standard large-BT result is coherence²/(B·T), which trigamma(B·T) exceeds by about 1/(2(BT)²) (5% at BT = 10, 14% at BT = 3.5, the slow band at 1 s); the diagonal is exact. The statement describes what the code does, so this is a modeling approximation, not a misstatement. (2) The gamma shape B·T is the long-window approximation, as claim erd-detect says.
suggested_fix: Optional: 'the trigamma of B·T (close to 1/(B·T)) times the squared normalized cross-power'.
bibliographic_issues: Kay 1998 is Volume II (Detection Theory). The Bayesian linear model with Gaussian random amplitudes appears there in Section 5.4 ('Linear Model', after the estimator-correlator of 5.3, per a course outline that follows the book), but the general colored-noise form (M + Λ)⁻¹TᵀC⁻¹ is derived in Volume I (Estimation Theory, 1993; Theorem 10.3 and the Bayesian Gauss-Markov Theorem 12.1). Consider citing Volume I or adding 'Section 5.4' to the Volume II entry. The Condon & Ransom entry (Princeton University Press 2016; NRAO online text, section 3.6, eqs. 3.153-3.154) matches the batch-14 check; the URL could not be reached from this environment.

discrepancy: None in the arithmetic. The rule assumes each meta-analytic g is standardized by the between-person SD of (log) power; where a within-subject study standardizes by the SD of paired differences the implied change is smaller. quote: The first five sit at the vertex and at the front, back, left and right of the rim, like Cz, Fpz, Oz, T7 and T8.
